Hiyya replied that he ensures it is never forgotten: he grows flax for nets, traps deer, feeds orphans the meat, writes scrolls on the hides, and teaches each child one book or order to pass on to the others.

stories.actor: Rav Nahman's relative and her daughter
stories.event: A relative of Rav Nahman sold her ketuba rights, was divorced and died, and the buyers claimed it from her daughter.
stories.turn: Rav Nahman hinted aloud that the daughter could forgive the ketuba to her father and inherit it from him.
stories.outcome: She did so, and Rav Nahman later regretted acting like an advocate.
stories.summary: Rav Nahman's relative sold her marriage contract rights, then was divorced and died, and the buyers came to collect from her daughter. Rav Nahman remarked that someone should advise her to forgive the debt to her father and inherit it from him later; she heard and did so. Rav Nahman afterwards said he had made himself like a judge's advocate.

stories.actor: An Amorite and a resident of Eretz Yisrael
stories.event: The Amorite asked how much the palm by the Jordan yielded and heard sixty kor.
stories.turn: He mocked that they had ruined the land, since it once gave 120.
stories.outcome: The resident replied he meant one side only.
stories.summary: An Amorite asked an Israelite how many dates they harvested from a palm on the Jordan. Told sixty kor, he scoffed that they had already ruined the land, since his people took 120. The Israelite answered that he had counted only one side of the tree.

stories.actor: Rabbi Elazar
stories.event: He ascended to Eretz Yisrael, was ordained, and was appointed to the calendar council.
stories.turn: At each step he declared himself spared another curse.
stories.outcome: He escaped all three curses of the false prophets.
stories.summary: On arriving in Eretz Yisrael Rabbi Elazar said he was spared one curse, on ordination two, and on joining the intercalation council three.

stories.actor: Rabbi Zeira
stories.event: Going up to Eretz Yisrael he found no ferry and crossed the Jordan by a rope.
stories.turn: A Sadducee mocked the Jews as hasty.
stories.outcome: Rabbi Zeira answered that he hurried lest he lose a privilege denied Moses and Aaron.
stories.summary: Rabbi Zeira, finding no ferry, pulled himself across the Jordan on a rope. A Sadducee called the Jews a rash people, and Zeira replied that he could not be sure he would merit a land Moses and Aaron never entered.

stories.actor: A millstone owner and his renter
stories.event: A man rented a millstone in exchange for grinding services.
stories.turn: The owner grew rich, bought his own mill and donkey, and demanded money instead.
stories.outcome: The renter refused, saying he agreed only to grind.
stories.summary: A man rented out his millstone in return for grinding his grain. Once rich, he bought his own mill and demanded payment in money, but the renter insisted he had only agreed to grind for him.

stories.actor: Rabban Gamliel bar Rabbi and a couple
stories.event: A groom complained he found no blood and the bride said she was a virgin.
stories.turn: Rabban Gamliel tested two maidservants on a wine barrel and then the bride.
stories.outcome: The wine scent did not pass through her, and he told the groom to take his acquisition.
stories.summary: A groom came to Rabban Gamliel bar Rabbi saying he found no blood; the bride insisted she was a virgin. Gamliel seated a virgin and non-virgin maidservant on a wine barrel to test the method, then the bride, whose breath carried no wine scent, and ruled her a virgin.

stories.actor: Rabban Gamliel the Elder and a couple
stories.event: A groom found no blood and the bride said she was of the Dorketi family, who have none.
stories.turn: Rabban Gamliel investigated her relatives and found it true.
stories.outcome: He told the groom to take his acquisition and called him fortunate.
stories.summary: A groom complained to Rabban Gamliel the Elder that he found no blood. The bride said her family, the Dorketi, have neither menstrual nor hymeneal blood; Gamliel checked her relatives, confirmed it, and told the groom to keep her.

stories.actor: Rabbi Yehuda HaNasi and a couple
stories.event: A groom found no blood and the bride said she was a virgin, during a famine.
stories.turn: Rabbi saw their faces were black with hunger and had them bathed and fed.
stories.outcome: The groom then found blood, and Rabbi told him to take his acquisition.
stories.summary: During years of drought a groom told Rabbi he found no blood while the bride maintained her virginity. Noticing they were starved, Rabbi had them bathed, fed and sent to a room; the groom then found blood, and Rabbi quoted a verse about skin shriveled on bones.

stories.actor: Rabbi Zeira and Rava in Mehoza
stories.event: Rabbi Zeira taught that a convert may marry a mamzeret and the converts pelted him with etrogim.
stories.turn: Rava taught that a convert may marry a priest's daughter and was carried on silk, then repeated the mamzeret ruling.
stories.outcome: When the people complained, Rava said he had given them both options.
stories.summary: Rabbi Zeira taught in Mehoza that a convert may marry a mamzeret, and the many converts there stoned him with etrogim. Rava then taught that a convert may marry a priest's daughter and was carried on silk, but later also taught the mamzeret ruling; to their protest he answered he had done them good, letting them marry from either group.

stories.actor: Rabbi Yohanan's relatives
stories.event: They seized an orphans' cow for a debt and Rabbi Yohanan approved.
stories.turn: Reish Lakish told them to return it.
stories.outcome: Rabbi Yohanan said he could do nothing, as his equal disagreed.
stories.summary: Rabbi Yohanan's relatives seized a cow belonging to orphans and he told them they had done well. Reish Lakish ordered them to give it back, and when they returned to Rabbi Yohanan he said he could not overrule a peer who disagreed with him.

stories.actor: An orphans' herdsman and a creditor
stories.event: A creditor seized an ox from the herdsman and claimed he took it before the debtor died.
stories.turn: The herdsman said it was after, and they went to Rav Nahman.
stories.outcome: With no witnesses to the seizure, Rav Nahman believed the creditor.
stories.summary: A creditor took an ox from the herdsman of some orphans, claiming he seized it while their father lived; the herdsman said it was after his death. Rav Nahman asked for witnesses to the seizure, and when there were none, ruled the creditor credible.

stories.actor: The house of the Nasi and the judges
stories.event: The Nasi's household seized an orphans' maidservant, and Rabbi Abbahu approved.
stories.turn: Rabbi Abba accused the judges of flattering the Nasi's house, citing Reish Lakish's reversal.
stories.outcome: The window ends with Rabbi Abba's rebuke.
stories.summary: Members of the Nasi's house seized a maidservant of orphans for a debt, and Rabbi Abbahu told them they had done well. Rabbi Abba challenged the judges for currying favor, recalling that Reish Lakish had reversed such a ruling.

stories.actor: A son-in-law and Rav Sheshet
stories.event: A son-in-law passed by his father-in-law's door.
stories.turn: There were rumors about him and his mother-in-law.
stories.outcome: Rav Sheshet had him flogged.
stories.summary: A son-in-law walked past his father-in-law's house, and because of rumors linking him with his mother-in-law, Rav Sheshet flogged him.

stories.actor: A man betrothing with a myrtle mat
stories.event: He betrothed a woman with a mat of myrtle.
stories.turn: Told it was worth less than a peruta, he said she should be betrothed with the four dinars inside it.
stories.outcome: She took it silently, and Rava ruled the silence meaningless.
stories.summary: A man betrothed a woman with a myrtle mat, and bystanders objected it was worthless. He declared she should be betrothed by the four dinars wrapped in it; she took it and said nothing, and Rava ruled that silence after the money is given counts for nothing.

stories.actor: Rav Hiyya bar Adda and Reish Lakish
stories.event: The children's teacher was absent for three days.
stories.turn: He explained he was harvesting an enormously fruitful vine, whose yield fell each day.
stories.outcome: Reish Lakish told him it would have yielded more had he not neglected the children.
stories.summary: Rav Hiyya bar Adda, a teacher, stayed away three days, and Reish Lakish asked why. He said he was harvesting a vine left by his father, three hundred clusters a day, yielding less wine each day; Reish Lakish answered that his absence from teaching was why the yield shrank.

stories.actor: Rami bar Yehezkel
stories.event: Visiting Benei Berak he saw goats under fig trees.
stories.turn: Honey dripped from the figs and milk from the goats and they mixed.
stories.outcome: He declared this the meaning of 'flowing with milk and honey'.
stories.summary: Rami bar Yehezkel came to Benei Berak and saw goats grazing under figs, with honey oozing from the fruit and milk dripping from the goats into it. He said this was what 'a land flowing with milk and honey' means.

stories.actor: Rabbi Yehoshua and a questioner
stories.event: A man asked what the law is if one's mother is divorced.
stories.turn: Rabbi Yehoshua saw from his tears he was a widow's son.
stories.outcome: He answered sarcastically to pour water and call them like chickens.
stories.summary: A man asked Rabbi Yehoshua about honoring a divorced mother. Seeing from his tear-filled eyes that he was a widow's son, Rabbi Yehoshua mocked the question, telling him to pour water in a pitcher and cluck at his parents like chickens.

stories.actor: Dama ben Netina
stories.event: The Sages wanted to buy merchandise from him at a huge profit.
stories.turn: The key lay under his sleeping father's head.
stories.outcome: He did not wake his father and lost the sale.
stories.summary: Asked how far honoring parents goes, Rav Ulla told of Dama ben Netina of Ashkelon, a gentile. The Sages offered a deal worth 600,000 dinars, but the key was under his sleeping father's head and he would not disturb him.

stories.actor: Dama ben Netina
stories.event: He refused to wake his father to sell stones for the ephod.
stories.turn: The next year a red heifer was born in his herd.
stories.outcome: He asked the Sages only for the sum he had lost honoring his father.
stories.summary: Dama ben Netina gave up a sale of ephod stones rather than wake his father, who slept on the key. The following year God rewarded him with a red heifer; when the Sages came to buy it, he asked only for the money he had lost for his father's honor.

stories.actor: Dama ben Netina and his mother
stories.event: He sat in a gold cloak among the nobles of Rome.
stories.turn: His mother tore the cloak, struck his head and spat in his face.
stories.outcome: He did not shame her.
stories.summary: Once Dama ben Netina sat among Roman nobles in a golden cloak, and his mother came, tore it off, slapped him and spat at him. He did not humiliate her in return.

stories.actor: A launderer
stories.event: A Divine Voice declared all present at Rabbi's funeral destined for the World-to-Come, but a launderer who visited Rabbi daily had missed it.
stories.turn: Hearing of Rabbi's death, he threw himself from a roof and died.
stories.outcome: A Divine Voice declared he too was destined for the World-to-Come.
stories.summary: On the day of Rabbi's funeral a heavenly voice promised the World-to-Come to all who attended. A launderer who came to Rabbi every day had not come that day; on hearing the news he climbed to a roof, fell and died, and a heavenly voice declared that he too would have a share.

stories.actor: Mar Zutra and Rabbi Yehuda of India
stories.event: Mar Zutra visited the dying convert who had no heirs.
stories.turn: Seeing death near, he had the convert's slave carry his shoes home to acquire him.
stories.outcome: The convert died and Mar Zutra gained the slave.
stories.summary: Rabbi Yehuda of India, a convert without heirs, fell ill and Mar Zutra visited him. Seeing he was about to die, Mar Zutra told his slave to take off his shoes and carry them to his house, acquiring him; one departed to death and the other to life.

stories.actor: Shmuel
stories.event: A man helped Shmuel off a ferry.
stories.turn: The man said he had a case before him.
stories.outcome: Shmuel disqualified himself.
stories.summary: As Shmuel crossed on a ferry a man gave him a hand. When the man said he had a case pending, Shmuel declared himself disqualified from judging it.

stories.actor: Ameimar
stories.event: While he judged, a man removed a feather from his head.
stories.turn: The man had a case before him.
stories.outcome: Ameimar disqualified himself.
stories.summary: A feather landed on Ameimar's head as he sat in judgment and a man brushed it off. Learning the man had a case, Ameimar disqualified himself.

stories.actor: Mar Ukva
stories.event: A man covered spittle lying before Mar Ukva.
stories.turn: The man had a case before him.
stories.outcome: Mar Ukva disqualified himself.
stories.summary: A man covered some spittle in front of Mar Ukva. When he said he had a case, Mar Ukva declared himself unfit to judge it.

stories.actor: Rabbi Yishmael son of Rabbi Yosei
stories.event: His sharecropper brought the weekly fruit basket early, on Thursday.
stories.turn: He had a case that day; Rabbi Yishmael refused the fruit and appointed other judges, yet found himself rooting for him.
stories.outcome: He cursed bribe-takers, reasoning that real bribes must bias far more.
stories.summary: Rabbi Yishmael's sharecropper brought his fruit on Thursday instead of Friday because he had a case. Rabbi Yishmael refused the basket, disqualified himself and seated two other scholars, but caught himself thinking of arguments for the man. He exclaimed that if he who took nothing felt this, those who take bribes are far worse.

stories.actor: Rabbi Yishmael bar Elisha
stories.event: A man from afar brought him the first shearing.
stories.turn: He admitted he came because he had a case.
stories.outcome: Rabbi Yishmael refused the gift and disqualified himself.
stories.summary: A man brought the priest Rabbi Yishmael bar Elisha the first shearing from a distant town. Asked why he passed other priests, he said he had a case before him, and Rabbi Yishmael refused the gift and the case.

stories.actor: A man and a woman washing her feet
stories.event: He grabbed coins from another man and threw them to her, declaring her betrothed.
stories.turn: The case came before Rava.
stories.outcome: Rava ruled the betrothal void, since the coins were stolen.
stories.summary: A man snatched dinars from someone and threw them to a woman washing her feet, saying she was betrothed. Rava ruled that nobody follows Rabbi Shimon's view that the owner despairs, so the betrothal was void.

stories.actor: A sharecropper
stories.event: He betrothed a woman with a handful of onions from the field.
stories.turn: Rava asked who had permitted him to take them.
stories.outcome: The betrothal was invalid as stolen goods.
stories.summary: A sharecropper betrothed a woman with a handful of onions from the field he worked. Rava asked who had given them to him, implying they were stolen and the betrothal failed.

stories.actor: A brewer
stories.event: He betrothed a woman with beer sediment belonging to his employer.
stories.turn: The owner found him and asked why he had not used the better sediment.
stories.outcome: Rava ruled that this does not imply consent outside teruma.
stories.summary: A brewer betrothed a woman with sediment from his employer's beer. The owner caught him and asked why he hadn't used the sharper sediment; Rava ruled that such a remark shows consent only regarding teruma, so the brewer had no right to it.

stories.actor: A man in love
stories.event: He suffered for love of a woman and wanted to leave Eretz Yisrael.
stories.turn: He heard the teaching about the importance of the Land.
stories.outcome: He stayed and suffered until his death.
stories.summary: A man pining for a certain woman wanted to leave Eretz Yisrael. On hearing how important burial and life in the Land are, he stayed and endured his longing until the day he died.

stories.actor: Rabbi Yehuda HaNasi
stories.event: He arranged a match for his son with Rabbi Hiyya's family.
stories.turn: The bride died when the ketuba was being written.
stories.outcome: They examined lineage and found a difference in descent from David's line.
stories.summary: Rabbi arranged for his son to marry into Rabbi Hiyya's family, but the girl died as the marriage contract was being written. Fearing a flaw, they checked the families and found Rabbi descended from Shefatya son of Avital and Hiyya from Shimi, David's brother.

stories.actor: Rabbi's son
stories.event: Betrothed into Rabbi Yosei ben Zimra's family, he agreed to study twelve years before marrying.
stories.turn: After seeing the bride he cut it to six years, then married first, and was ashamed before his father.
stories.outcome: His father reassured him, then he studied twelve years; his wife became infertile and he prayed and she was cured.
stories.summary: Rabbi's son was to study twelve years before marrying a daughter of Yosei ben Zimra. Seeing her, he reduced it to six, then insisted on marrying first, and felt ashamed; Rabbi told him he had acted like God, who brought the Sanctuary forward. He then studied twelve years, returned to find her infertile, and prayed until she was healed.

stories.actor: Rabbi Hananya ben Hakhinai
stories.event: He left for twelve years of study without waiting for Rabbi Shimon.
stories.turn: Returning, he found home by following his daughter, and his wife died of shock.
stories.outcome: He prayed and she revived.
stories.summary: Hananya ben Hakhinai studied away for twelve years and on returning could not find his house. He followed a girl called 'daughter of Hakhinai' home; his wife saw him and died of shock, and he prayed and she lived.

stories.actor: Rabbi Hama bar Bisa
stories.event: Returning after twelve years, he went to the study hall first and sent word home.
stories.turn: A sharp young scholar questioned him, and he regretted not having a son like that.
stories.outcome: The window ends with his regret.
stories.summary: Hama bar Bisa, avoiding Ben Hakhinai's mistake, waited in the local study hall after twelve years away. His own son Oshaya, unrecognized, came and debated with him, and Hama lamented that had he been home he would have had such a child.

stories.actor: Rabbi Tarfon and Rabbi Akiva
stories.event: A mikveh in Yavne presumed full was measured and found deficient, raising the status of earlier purifications.
stories.turn: Tarfon ruled them pure and Akiva impure; they traded parables until Akiva's analysis prevailed.
stories.outcome: Tarfon conceded, saying whoever parts from Akiva parts from life.
stories.summary: A reservoir in Yavne thought to hold forty se'a was found short, and Rabbi Tarfon and Rabbi Akiva disputed the purity of everything immersed in it. Each offered a parable about a disqualified priest; Akiva showed his comparison fit better, and Tarfon conceded with praise for him.

stories.actor: Abaye
stories.event: Abaye rode along the bank of the Sagya River while Rav Mesharshiyya and other rabbis sat on the far bank and did not stand for him.
stories.turn: Abaye challenged them for not standing before their primary teacher.
stories.outcome: They answered that they had not seen him at all.
stories.summary: Abaye was riding his donkey along the Sagya River, and Rav Mesharshiyya and other rabbis on the other bank did not rise. He asked them whether he was not their primary teacher, owed honor even from afar. They replied that they had not noticed him.

stories.actor: Ravina and Rabbi Yirmeya of Difti
stories.event: While Ravina sat before Rabbi Yirmeya, a man passed by without covering his head.
stories.turn: Ravina called the man rude.
stories.outcome: Rabbi Yirmeya suggested the man was from Mata Mehasya, where rabbis are so common that people are less careful to honor them.
stories.summary: Ravina was sitting before Rabbi Yirmeya of Difti when a man walked past without covering his head. Ravina remarked on how rude he was. Rabbi Yirmeya excused him, suggesting he came from Mata Mehasya, where rabbis are commonplace.

stories.actor: Rav Shmuel bar Rav Yitzhak
stories.event: Rav Shmuel bar Rav Yitzhak juggled three myrtle branches while dancing before brides.
stories.turn: Rabbi Zeira complained that the old man was humiliating the scholars, but at his death a pillar of fire separated him from everyone else.
stories.outcome: Rabbi Zeira conceded that the old man's branch (or folly, or method) had earned him this honor.
stories.summary: Rav Shmuel bar Rav Yitzhak used to dance before brides juggling three myrtle branches, and Rabbi Zeira thought it demeaned the Sages. When Rav Shmuel died, a pillar of fire, granted to only one or two people in a generation, separated him from everyone. Rabbi Zeira then admitted that his dancing had earned him this reward.

stories.actor: King Agrippa
stories.event: King Agrippa rerouted his entourage to yield before a bride's wedding procession.
stories.turn: He did so although a king is not required to yield.
stories.outcome: The Sages praised him.
stories.summary: Although a king of Israel takes precedence over a wedding procession, King Agrippa stepped aside for a bride. The Sages praised him for it.

stories.actor: A woman and the child she raised
stories.event: A woman came to Jerusalem with a child on her shoulders and raised him.
stories.turn: When grown, he had intercourse with her.
stories.outcome: They were brought to court and stoned, on the presumption that he was her son.
stories.summary: A woman arrived in Jerusalem carrying a child on her shoulders and raised him as her own. Later he had relations with her. The court stoned them both, not because he was definitely her son but because he had always clung to her as one.

stories.actor: Hillel the Elder
stories.event: Hillel provided a formerly wealthy poor man with a horse and a servant to run before him.
stories.turn: Once no servant could be found.
stories.outcome: Hillel himself ran before the man for three mil.
stories.summary: Hillel the Elder supplied an impoverished man of noble family with a horse to ride and a servant to run ahead of him. One day no servant was available. Hillel ran ahead of him himself for three mil.

stories.actor: Rabbi Nehemya and a poor man
stories.event: A poor man who was used to fatty meat and aged wine asked Rabbi Nehemya for charity.
stories.turn: Rabbi Nehemya invited him to share his lentils, and the man died after eating them.
stories.outcome: Rabbi Nehemya lamented the man, blaming the man's own excessive indulgence.
stories.summary: A man came to Rabbi Nehemya for charity and said he usually dined on fatty meat and aged wine. Rabbi Nehemya asked him to share his own meal of lentils; the man ate and died. Rabbi Nehemya said 'Woe to this one killed by Nehemya,' meaning the man should not have pampered himself so.

stories.actor: Rava and a poor man
stories.event: A poor man asked Rava for charity and said he ate fattened hen and aged wine.
stories.turn: When Rava rebuked him for burdening the community, the man said God provides each person's food; just then Rava's sister, unseen for thirteen years, arrived bringing fattened hen and aged wine.
stories.outcome: Rava conceded to the man and invited him to eat.
stories.summary: A man seeking charity told Rava he dined on fattened hen and aged wine, and Rava asked whether he cared about the community's burden. The man replied that he ate from God, not from them. At that moment Rava's sister, whom he had not seen for thirteen years, arrived with exactly a fattened hen and aged wine. Rava told the man he had been answered and invited him to eat.

stories.actor: Rabbi Hanina bar Pappi
stories.event: A noblewoman tried to seduce Rabbi Hanina bar Pappi; he covered himself with boils by incantation, she healed him by magic, and he fled to a demon-haunted bathhouse.
stories.turn: He survived the night unharmed in the dangerous bathhouse.
stories.outcome: He told the Sages two imperial soldiers guarded him, and they explained that one who resists forbidden intercourse is granted a miracle.
stories.summary: A noblewoman propositioned Rabbi Hanina bar Pappi, so he used an incantation to cover himself in boils, but she healed him with magic. He fled and hid in a bathhouse so dangerous that even two people together were harmed there by day. The next day he told the Sages that two imperial guards had protected him all night, and they concluded that a miracle is done for one who escapes forbidden intercourse.

stories.actor: Rabbi Tzadok
stories.event: A noblewoman tried to seduce Rabbi Tzadok, and he stalled by asking for food; she offered non-kosher food and put it in the oven.
stories.turn: He climbed into the burning oven, saying that one who commits this sin falls into fire.
stories.outcome: She said that had she known how seriously he took it she would not have troubled him.
stories.summary: When a noblewoman propositioned Rabbi Tzadok, he said he was too weak and asked for food. She offered non-kosher food and lit the oven to roast it, and he climbed into the oven, explaining that one who commits such a sin falls into fire. She told him that had she known it mattered so much, she would not have pressed him.

stories.actor: Rav Kahana
stories.event: A noblewoman tried to seduce Rav Kahana, a basket seller, and he excused himself to adorn himself.
stories.turn: He went up to the roof and threw himself off, and Elijah came and caught him.
stories.outcome: Elijah complained of traveling four hundred parasangs; Rav Kahana blamed poverty, and Elijah gave him a basket of dinars.
stories.summary: Rav Kahana sold baskets, and a noblewoman propositioned him. He said he would go prepare himself, climbed to the roof and jumped. Elijah the prophet caught him and complained of the four-hundred-parasang trip; Rav Kahana answered that poverty had put him in that position, and Elijah gave him a basket full of dinars.

stories.actor: A woman, Rav Nahman, Rav Anan and Mar Ukva
stories.event: A woman about to remarry deeded her property to her daughter to keep it from her new husband, then was divorced and wanted it back.
stories.turn: Rav Nahman tore up the daughter's deed, and Rav Anan complained to Mar Ukva that Rav Nahman tears up people's documents.
stories.outcome: On hearing the facts, Mar Ukva cited Shmuel's ruling that a document of evasion should be torn, vindicating Rav Nahman.
stories.summary: Before remarrying, a woman wrote her property over to her daughter to shield it from her husband; after she was divorced, she wanted it back. Rav Nahman tore the deed. Rav Anan went to Mar Ukva to complain about 'Nahman the farmer' destroying documents, but when Mar Ukva heard the details he cited Shmuel: a document of evasion is to be torn.

stories.actor: A depositor and Rabbi Ami
stories.event: A man deposited seven pearls wrapped in a sheet with Rabbi Meyasha, who died without leaving instructions.
stories.turn: The depositor and the heirs disputed ownership before Rabbi Ami.
stories.outcome: Rabbi Ami awarded the pearls to the depositor, since Rabbi Meyasha was not wealthy and the depositor gave an identifying mark.
stories.summary: A man left seven pearls tied in a sheet at the house of Rabbi Meyasha, grandson of Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi, who then died without saying whose they were. The parties came before Rabbi Ami. He ruled for the claimant, because Rabbi Meyasha could not have afforded such pearls and the claimant identified them by a sign.

stories.actor: A depositor and Rav Nahman
stories.event: A man deposited a silver goblet with Hasa, who died without instructions.
stories.turn: The case came before Rav Nahman.
stories.outcome: Rav Nahman awarded it to the depositor, since Hasa was not wealthy and the depositor gave an identifying mark.
stories.summary: A man deposited a silver goblet with Hasa, who died without leaving word about it. Rav Nahman heard the case. He gave the goblet to the claimant, noting that Hasa was not wealthy and that the claimant could identify it.

stories.actor: A depositor and Rabbi Abba
stories.event: A man deposited silk with Rav Dimi, brother of Rav Safra, who died without instructions.
stories.turn: The case came before Rabbi Abba.
stories.outcome: Rabbi Abba awarded the silk to the depositor, since Rav Dimi was not wealthy and the depositor gave an identifying mark.
stories.summary: A man deposited silk with Rav Dimi, who died without saying whose it was. Rabbi Abba heard the dispute. He ruled for the claimant, since Rav Dimi was not wealthy and the claimant gave a distinguishing mark.

stories.actor: A dying man and Toviya
stories.event: A dying man said his property should go to Toviya.
stories.turn: After his death a Toviya came to claim it.
stories.outcome: Rabbi Yohanan ruled that Toviya had come and could take it.
stories.summary: A man on his deathbed left his property to 'Toviya' and then died. A man named Toviya arrived to claim it. Rabbi Yohanan ruled that this Toviya was the heir, with no concern that another Toviya was meant.

stories.actor: Ravin the Pious
stories.event: Ravin went as agent to betroth a woman to his son.
stories.turn: Her family refused the son, so Ravin betrothed her to himself without informing his son.
stories.outcome: He married her himself, fearing someone else would betroth her in the meantime.
stories.summary: Ravin the Pious went to arrange his son's betrothal to a woman, but ended up betrothing her to himself. Her family would not give her to the son, only to the father. He did not first tell his son, fearing another suitor would take her meanwhile.

stories.actor: Rav and Rabba bar bar Hana
stories.event: Rabba bar bar Hana gave Rav money to buy a certain field for him.
stories.turn: Rav bought it for himself instead, because the violent locals would sell to Rav but not to Rabba bar bar Hana.
stories.outcome: Rav kept the land, acting without informing him lest someone else buy it first.
stories.summary: Rabba bar bar Hana gave Rav money to buy a field for him, and Rav bought it for himself. The field lay in a valley of violent men who respected Rav but not Rabba bar bar Hana. Rav did not stop to tell him, fearing another buyer would take it in the meantime.

stories.actor: Rav Giddel and Rabbi Abba
stories.event: Rabbi Abba bought a field Rav Giddel was negotiating for, and Rav Giddel complained up the chain to Rav Yitzhak Nappaha.
stories.turn: Confronted at the Festival, Rabbi Abba said he had not known, and refused to sell his first land but offered it as a gift.
stories.outcome: Rav Giddel would not accept a gift and Rabbi Abba would not use it, so it became known as 'the land of the Sages'.
stories.summary: Rav Giddel was negotiating for a field when Rabbi Abba bought it; Rav Giddel complained to Rabbi Zeira, who took it to Rav Yitzhak Nappaha. At the Festival Rav Yitzhak asked Rabbi Abba about a pauper whose loaf is snatched, and Rabbi Abba agreed the snatcher is wicked, said he had not known, and offered the land as a gift since he would not sell his first purchase. Rav Giddel refused gifts and Rabbi Abba would not use it, so neither took the field and it was called the land of the Sages.

stories.actor: Rabbi Hananya ben Hakhinai
stories.event: Returning home after many years, he recognized his daughter by hearing her called by name at the river and followed her home.
stories.turn: His wife saw him suddenly and died of the shock.
stories.outcome: He prayed for her and she was revived.
stories.summary: Sitting by the river, Rabbi Hananya heard a girl called 'daughter of Hakhinai' and realized she was his own daughter, so he followed her home. His wife, sifting flour, looked up, saw him, and died from the shock. He protested to God that this could not be her reward, prayed for mercy, and she lived.

stories.actor: Rabbi Hama bar Bisa
stories.event: After twelve years in the study hall, Rabbi Hama went first to his hometown study hall rather than surprising his wife, and a sharp young scholar questioned him.
stories.turn: He regretted that he had no such son, then stood up for the young man at home, not realizing it was his own son Oshaya.
stories.outcome: His wife asked whether a father stands for his son, revealing the truth.
stories.summary: Rabbi Hama bar Bisa studied away for twelve years and, to avoid what happened to ben Hakhinai, sent word home from the local study hall. A brilliant young man questioned him, and Rabbi Hama lamented that had he been home he could have had a son like that. When the young man followed him home and Rabbi Hama rose before him, his wife asked whether a father stands before his son: it was his son, Rabbi Oshaya.

stories.actor: Rabbi Akiva and his wife
stories.event: The daughter of ben Kalba Savua betrothed herself to his shepherd Akiva on condition he study, and her father disowned her by vow.
stories.turn: Akiva studied twenty-four years, returned with twenty-four thousand students, and honored her before all; her father came seeking release from his vow.
stories.outcome: Learning the great man was Akiva, ben Kalba Savua bowed to him and gave him half his wealth.
stories.summary: Ben Kalba Savua's daughter saw the shepherd Akiva's worth, betrothed herself to him in secret and sent him to study; her father threw her out and vowed she would get nothing of his. Akiva studied twelve years, overheard her say she would wish him to study twelve more, and did so, returning with twenty-four thousand students; when she fell at his feet he told his students that all their learning was hers. Her father, coming to the great sage to annul his vow, said he would never have vowed had he thought Akiva would learn anything, and on learning who he was fell at his feet and gave him half his wealth. Akiva's daughter later did the same for ben Azzai.

stories.actor: Rav Yosef son of Rava
stories.event: Rav Yosef, sent to study for six years, left after three to visit his wife on Yom Kippur eve.
stories.turn: His father came out armed to meet him and rebuked him for remembering his wife.
stories.outcome: The quarrel kept them both from eating the meal before the fast.
stories.summary: Rava sent his son Rav Yosef to study for six years, but after three years, on the eve of Yom Kippur, the son set out to visit his wife. Rava took a weapon and went to meet him, asking scornfully whether he had remembered his woman. In the quarrel, neither of them ate the final meal before the fast.

stories.actor: Ravina
stories.event: Ravina held wine belonging to his orphaned nephew and was taking his own wine to Sikhra to sell.
stories.turn: He asked Rav Ashi whether he could take the orphan's wine along.
stories.outcome: Rav Ashi told him to go, since the orphan's wine was no better than his own.
stories.summary: Ravina was looking after wine belonging to his orphaned nephew, Ravina the younger, and was taking his own wine to sell in Sikhra. He asked Rav Ashi whether he could bring the orphan's wine too. Rav Ashi told him to go ahead, since the orphan's wine deserved no better treatment than his own.

stories.actor: Rava and a divorced betrothed couple
stories.event: A betrothed couple who had divorced came before Rava for a money judgment.
stories.turn: Rava placed an intermediary between them, and Rav Adda bar Mattana objected citing the rule that betrothed parties may deal directly.
stories.outcome: Rava answered that this couple were plainly familiar with each other; another version reverses who proposed and who objected.
stories.summary: A divorced betrothed man and woman came before Rava, with Rav Adda bar Mattana present. Rava put an intermediary between them, and Rav Adda objected that, by a teaching in Evel Rabbati, betrothed people need no go-between. Rava replied that he could see these two were familiar with each other; in another version Rav Adda urged the intermediary and gave that reply himself.

stories.actor: Rabbi Yonatan and a father
stories.event: A man bowed and kissed Rabbi Yonatan's foot in front of Rabbi Hanina.
stories.turn: Rabbi Hanina asked why, and Rabbi Yonatan explained that the man had signed his property over to his sons.
stories.outcome: Rabbi Yonatan had forced the sons to support him, which earned his gratitude.
stories.summary: While Rabbi Hanina and Rabbi Yonatan stood together, a man bent down and kissed Rabbi Yonatan's foot. Rabbi Hanina asked what it meant. Rabbi Yonatan said the man had written his property over to his sons and he had compelled them to feed him.

stories.actor: Rabbi Yeshevav (or a certain man) and his friend
stories.event: A man sought to give more than a fifth of his property to charity.
stories.turn: His friend stepped in.
stories.outcome: The friend did not let him; it was either Rabbi Yeshevav stopping someone, or Rabbi Akiva stopping Rabbi Yeshevav.
stories.summary: Someone wanted to give away more than a fifth of his property to charity, and his friend would not allow it. In one version the friend was Rabbi Yeshevav; in another, Rabbi Yeshevav was the giver and Rabbi Akiva stopped him.

stories.actor: Rabbi Ami and a witness
stories.event: A man told Rabbi Ami that another had presumptive status as a priest because he read first from the Torah.
stories.turn: Rabbi Ami asked whether that was as a priest or as a great man, and the witness said a Levite read after him.
stories.outcome: Rabbi Ami elevated the man to the priesthood on his word.
stories.summary: A man testified to Rabbi Ami that someone was a presumed priest because he was called first to the Torah. Rabbi Ami asked whether that might be because he was a prominent man, and the witness answered that a Levite read after him. Rabbi Ami confirmed his priesthood on that testimony.

stories.actor: Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi and a witness
stories.event: A man told Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi that another was a presumed Levite because he read second from the Torah.
stories.turn: Asked whether that was as a Levite or as a great man, the witness said a priest read before him.
stories.outcome: Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi confirmed him as a Levite on his word.
stories.summary: A man testified before Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi that someone was a Levite because he read second in synagogue. The rabbi asked whether he might simply be prominent, and the witness said a priest had read first. Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi then established him as a Levite.

stories.actor: Reish Lakish and Rabbi Elazar
stories.event: When a witness claimed someone was a priest for reading first, Reish Lakish demanded proof he received teruma at the threshing floor, and Rabbi Elazar asked whether priesthood ends where there is no threshing floor.
stories.turn: Later the same case came before Rabbi Yohanan, who gave Rabbi Elazar's exact answer.
stories.outcome: Reish Lakish glared at Rabbi Elazar for citing Rabbi Yohanan's words without naming him.
stories.summary: Reish Lakish insisted that a priest's status be proven by his share of teruma at the threshing floor, and Rabbi Elazar retorted that priesthood cannot depend on there being a threshing floor. Later, sitting before Rabbi Yohanan, a similar case arose and Rabbi Yohanan gave the same retort. Reish Lakish looked harshly at Rabbi Elazar and rebuked him for repeating Rabbi Yohanan's teaching without attributing it, since he would have accepted it then.
